title: if your heart should ever slowly turn
creator: Lee Sharks
description:
This record preserves the complete textual manifestation of Lee Sharks’s five-line lyric *if your heart should ever slowly turn*. The poem imagines a beloved awakening slowly and astonished into a renewed world. Its final declaration—“then know / that I have loved you”—places love outside possession or response: the beloved’s future recognition is enough to carry the speaker’s past and continuing regard.

The text is the accessible and searchable counterpart to the image manifestation in #733. Punctuation and lineation are load-bearing, particularly the double-dash interruptions around “slowly, astonished,” the unfolding image of leaves unbundling from rain, and the isolated movement into “then know.” The authority description should preserve the poem’s lowercase title and avoid converting the lyric into biographical evidence about any named relationship.

wiki_article:
**if your heart should ever slowly turn** is a lyric poem by Lee Sharks, deposited on May 17, 2026.

The poem addresses a possible future awakening. A heart turns from sheltering sleep, leaves open after rain, and the world appears newly made. The speaker does not demand return, explanation, or immediate recognition. The closing lines ask only that, in such a moment, the beloved know they have been loved.

The poem is preserved in two forms. This record contains the searchable text; record #733 contains an image-borne presentation. The two should be cited as alternate manifestations.

Its short form depends on exact lineation and punctuation. The poem should be reproduced from the canonical body rather than from a prose paraphrase or an OCR-derived version.
